contractCorrections.target: dispatching-subagents-claude-draft.md — Selection Rule 4 and the prose 'Claude's OAT-managed dispatch axis is model, not a separate reasoning-effort axis'
contractCorrections.detail: effort_axis=not-applicable holds only for the native Agent tool, which has no effort parameter. `claude --effort <low|medium|high|xhigh|max>` exists on the CLI and Workflow.agent() accepts opts.effort with the same five values. The rule must be scoped per-surface.

Native model selection is tier-alias granularity only: the enum is exactly [sonnet, opus, haiku, fable], with no dated model IDs. A resolver returning an exact ID such as claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 cannot pass it through native dispatch; only the CLI accepts exact IDs. 'Exact model candidate' must be defined per-surface.

contractCorrections.correctionNote: Corrected 2026-07-11T21:06:29Z after direct probing (supplementary packet claude-2026-07-11T210629Z). A `Task` grant DOES resolve: it materializes the dispatch tool, which the child sees under its live name `Agent`. Controls confirm it — a ["Read"]-only grant yields a Read-only child (grant is enforced), and a bogus name is silently dropped (a surviving name was recognized, not echoed). oat-phase-implementer receives a working dispatch tool. Only cosmetic naming drift survives. Residual unprobed risk: unknown tool names are dropped WITHOUT error, so removal of the `Task` alias would fail silently; migrating the grant to `Agent` is robustness insurance, not a bug fix.
